title: A field extension gives an fpqc singleton cover of spectra
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. The structure morphism $p:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Consequently the one-member family $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: Topologies, Definition Tag 022B and Lemma Tag 03L7 (recognizing a singleton fpqc covering); flatness of a field extension is Algebra, Tag 00HB

proof.text: Mathlib infers flatness of p from its instance for morphisms to a subsingleton integral scheme. Spec k is a subsingleton integral scheme because k is a field. This realizes lem-pc-field-extension-flat.

Mathlib infers surjectivity of p from its instance for a nonempty source and a subsingleton target. Spec K is nonempty and Spec k is subsingleton because K and k are fields. This realizes lem-pc-field-extension-surjective.

Mathlib infers quasi-compactness of p because a morphism between affine schemes is affine and an affine morphism is quasi-compact. Both spectra are affine. This realizes lem-pc-field-extension-quasi-compact.

Apply Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.singleton_mem_fpqcPrecoverage to p, with the Flat, Surjective and QuasiCompact instances from Steps 1-3. This generic singleton criterion gives membership in fpqcPrecoverage, the Mathlib definition realizing def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering.
